They arrive and all scp's are contained except Scp 5133 where they report that it is memetic. item.title: [Seeking Greenlight] Host of the Eldritch Abomination.
item.content:encoded:
Seeking Greenlights:** Yes.

Page Type: SCP Article

Genre: Horror/Comedy

Elevator Pitch: A teenager name "Janual Grey" that one day discovers that he's no longer human after an unexplained blackout while he and his friends are at Acadia National Park, and later on woke up and finds himself as a space, time, and reality-altering eldritch abomination.

+ show block

Janual still acts like a regular human. However, discovering his powers has made a few changes. He begins to possess numerous anomalous properties that not even he knows how many does he has. Every 24 hours passes by. If Janual doesn't consume any food that gives him the nutrition he needs, he will get driven into a state of absolute hostility, where he would go on a never-ending frenzy to satisfy his hunger, which of course that time he would begin to use more of his anomalous properties to lure humans deep into the woods. Which is why he usually lures bad peoples into his territory and consumes them.


Central Narrative:
+ show block
– hide block

The main point here is that:

Janual wasn't actually a human at all. Janual was originally born like this already. His father was a cosmic eldritch deity worshiped by a cult named "Servants of "Darkness" " secretly built under a church where his mother as a nun is, the cult mainly focuses on worshiping a deity named "Darkness". When the cult let his father manifest into reality, he disguised himself as a handsome human and seduced his mother into having a child. After borning out Janual, he de-manifested himself out of reality to let his son, Janual, destroy the world instead of him. However, due to embodying human natures, Janual didn't become malevolent as his father was.

After a few years, when Janual's mother has raised him, she had witnessed him consume their neighbors in his monstrous form. As she started to find answers to why her son is like this, she soon discovers the truth. She could find a way to seal his powers from being unleashed due to worrying that he might bring apocalyptic events. However, during the past years, she slowly forgets that she must check and renew the seal.


Hook/Attention-Grabber: Janual is a friend in school with SCP-105 and is familiar with SCP-4051 as they've met each other before being held in Foundation custody.

item.title: Unvirtual Reality
item.description: A program that will help the SCP foundation combat and learn about other SCPs, at the cost of putting others and themselves in danger.
item.content:encoded:
Seeking Greenlights: Yes

Page Type: SCP Article. Several experimental test logs added as well.

Genre: Sci-fi, Parallel Universes

Elevator Pitch: SCP-XXXX is a computer program that one day appeared and automatically installed in every computer at site-XX. If run it will display the message "SCP Breach Simulator- Site XX Edition" and then create a realistic simulation of site XX, were you will play as yourself and will have to survive a SCP breach.

Central Narrative: Any computer brought into site-XX will manifest the program inside of their files, even if the computer was completely cut out from the internet and any other method of networking. SCP-XXXX cannot be deleted but any computer that is taken outside of the site will have the program erased from its files. SCP-XXXX will work on personal computers and laptops; smartphones, tablets, servers and mainframes won't manifest the program inside of their files. On the other hand anything that classifies as a personal computer, regardless of its model, year of manufacture or Operating System will manifest and be able to run the program. Older models will create more crude simulations, with very old computers generating text based descriptions and allowing the users to chose how to act with input prompts and more modern computers generating 3D environment that can even be compatible with Virtual Reality technology.

+ show block
– hide block

Hook/Attention Grabber: The program manifested after a particularly sudden and gruesome containment breach. In that breach agent XXXX mentioned how it felt as if her actions were not her own, but chosen and forced upon her by someone else. It is believed that the simulations that the SCP generates are not simulations at all, but live feed from a parallel universe where a breach is occurring. Players from this universe take control of their versions from the universe that is being shown in the computer, and the simulation will run until the breach is contained, the SCP escapes or the "player" dies. It is believed that after running a simulation SCP-XXXX will automatically install in every computer of site-XX of that particular parallel universe, spreading itself further and further.

The foundation can choose to use the SCP to conduct breaching simulations or even spy in parallel universes and steal research or information that might help their cause, but at the cost of damaging another SCP foundation from a parallel universe and spreading the SCP more and more. The more the SCP has spread the higher the chances are for the Foundation of this universe from becoming another "simulation" and suffering a breach.

item.title: Vague Memories
item.description: A phenomena that causes a person or thing to become unnaturally vague in what they're saying.
item.content:encoded:
Seeking Greenlights: Yes

Page Type: SCP Article

Genre: Mystery

Elevator Pitch: Documents, people, writings, anything infected with the SCP becomes very unnaturally vague, but doesn't cause any other harmful side effect.

Central Narrative: The phenomena is referred to as "Vagueing" or "The Vague".

The SCP isn't a state of matter, nor does it exist physically, rather it's a strange unknown phenomena that spreads from person to person, only when they share ideas, brainstorm together, etc. It effects a person's speaking, and causes them to speak rather vague.

Not only does it effect humans, but also effects documents and anything written by "Vagued Men". Such infected manuscripts include a lost SCP-001 article, and the "11th" commandment. It has the same exact effects, causing very slurred and vague text.

The SCP does not have any other side effects, and only causes slurring in speech, and unnatural vagueness, no nausea, no coughing, no death, nothing like that.

Hook/Attention Grabber: Basic idea yet has a lot of interesting details when it comes to "documents lost to the vague".

item.title: The White Glove's Limousine
item.content:encoded:
Seeking Greenlights : Yes

Page type : SCP Article

Genre : Drama/Mystery/Horror?

Elevator Pitch :

- An SCP that takes the form of a Mercedes-Maybach S600 Pullman Guard

- It usually appears in a handful of locations between 7 p.m. and 9 p.m, especially when the streets are crowded.

- The SCP will “target” a person out on their own, from the crowd, who will then feel obligated to seek out the car. Upon the target’s approach, a single hand wearing a white glove will emerge from the interior of the vehicle and will gesture for them to get inside.

- Once the person does so, the door will close violently. The car will then start moving again.

- It will disappear after 25 minutes of driving. A hypnotic effect distracts any human observing the car for too long after its departure. Recording the vehicle is impossible.

Narrative :

+ show block
– hide block

In 2010, the Foundation received reports of a series of mysterious disappearances around the Sydney Opera House, the Wynn and Encore complex, and the Théâtre de Paris. After long months of investigation, the dispatched agents discovered the source of the disappearances : a black limousine, presumed responsible for abducting the missing persons.

In order to determine its properties, it was deemed necessary to dispatch observation teams to all the destinations at which the anomalous limousine had been spotted. The O.T. located outside the Théâtre de Paris was the first to spot the limousine;, at 8 p.m, on the 19th of may 2010. Although the doors of the vehicle were opened upon arrival, its interior was impossible to observe due to a lack of light inside the car. A few minutes later, a Caucasian man in his 20s entered the limousine. The door then seemed to shut itself violently, and the car immediately took off. Attempts at following the object were always unsuccessful : after an average of 25 minutes of observation, any agent following the car experiences a brief moment of inattention, during which the vehicle escapes from view. Filming the vehicle also seems to be impossible : all video records in which the limousine appears seem to be heavily disturbed, and hence impossible to watch. If any person other than the target gets within arm’s reach of the vehicle, the doors will immediately clamp shut, and the car will flee the scene. To this day, this is the only known way to prevent further abductions by the object.

Attention-grabber : The mysterious limousine and disappearances.

Additional notes : None

item.title: In the blink of an eye
item.description: What you see defines what you can do, what if you could see *much more*?
item.content:encoded:
Seeking Greenlights: Yes

Page Type: SCP article/Personnel profile

Page Layout (Optional): Standard SCP page

Elevator Pitch:

  • Our senses define and limit how we interact with reality, they do not, however, define and limit reality itself. (aka there is more around us than meet the eye)
  • Human eyes can perceive three colors of light: red, blue and green, other colors are perceived by combining these three with the intensity of the light. Other animals have different light perception and therefore can see different colors than humans. Particularly, praying mantis shrimps can perceive between 12 and 16 light colors.
  • What happens when a human receives an experimental implant that allows them to see as many colors as a praying mantis shrimp?

Central Narrative: A high level MTF agent becomes blind after a mission and becomes the perfect guinea pig for an experimental biological implant that combines human and animal DNA to create augmented agents. The article starts with a brief description of the agent and how she lost her eyesight and how the implant was created. It follows with some logs regarding the surgery and recovery of the agent.

+ show block
– hide block

The meat of the narrative, though, is how her new eyes allow her to experience reality in a completely different way. Through personal entries on a journal she details her discoveries, they start small (new colors, night vision) and as she grows used to the new eyes they get bigger (she can see the flow of energy on living beings, see cracks and passages on reality that allow her to "teleport", see time as it passes, etc).

Hook/Attention-Grabber:

  • One goal here is create a new character to be used in future works on the wiki, she would make a great spy or extraction agent for example
  • Explore the growing sense of amazement and thrill someone feels when emerged on a new reality (aka my feelings when I discovered the SCP and plunged into this weird universe)
  • Expanding concepts such as the integrity of reality, time, space and other basic elements of the SCP universe and how humans and other beings interact with them

Additional Notes: None so far. Let the critiques begin!

item.title: SCP Concept: "This Last Week"
item.description: A town stuck looping the same week over and over again.
item.content:encoded:
Seeking Greenlights: Yes

Page Type: SCP Article

Genre: Drama/Emotional, possibly a little Horror (I think - hard to pin down)

Page Layout: Nothing incredibly special at this stage. If this ends up being my first published article, I don't want to be too ambitious and not be able to follow through without experience first.

Elevator Pitch: Time loop, town repeating for decades. No-one in town's aware it's happening.

Central Narrative: Loop - when first documented - lasted 1 week, resetting at midnight (internal date noted, but when undecided).

Log of events in cycle, taken not long into repeats. Includes local activities. Occasional person enters - unfortunates from before containment who didn't get out in time (e.g. Sole car enters. Driver confused because brother was in car in front, implying brother left town pre-midnight, while he didn't).

Affected bubble's temporal hazard, as anyone who enters becomes trapped in repeats if they don't leave pre-reset, arrival happening every time (shown with unfortunate agent). Living things from town cannot be removed, disappearing when extracted. Non-living objects can be, however, duplicates taking their place next repeat. Objects/people introduced from outside arrive at same time in later loops.

Speculated to be unstable spacetime bubble, causing repeats and leaking details from other realities, overwriting native. No cause determined.

+ show block
– hide block

Hook/Attention-Grabber: Subtle changes between loops - only couple tiny things in given repeat (e.g. teapot's colour or someone's breakfast). Small things eventually snowball into drastic shifts over countless cycles - e.g. street names, businesses and even identities (extreme example's bartender originally documented as male replaced by woman). Log of noted changes over time provided, starting out with small things before they're moved to unseen comprehensive file, log's remainder focusing on significant alterations.

Article end: Researcher contacts superior. Too subtle to tell before, but they're now sure loop's shrinking. Not physical space, but timeframe, and events aren't exiting the loop - they're compressing, events getting closer together and causing problems. Example: Car driving through crossroads, another driving from other road seconds after. Compressed, crossings get closer until cross at same time, and either stop or crash. Regardless, it's a major change, causing butterflies. They speculate that as bubble grows increasingly unstable, timeframe will keep shrinking, events compacting until "casual density event" occurs. It's anybody's guess what happens then. As it isn't accelerating, however - and week's only shortened by minutes in decades - it's centuries before "event". It's suggested personnel prepare in case something emerges sooner.

'Emerges' is deliberate wording. Speculation that distortion/timeline leakage caused by something pushing into our reality.

Compression's resulted in short calm immediately pre-midnight, where there's no more events. Town disappears temporarily, leaving semi-circular crater. Was emergence of this that revealed compression.

Additional Notes: Still trying to get SCP approved, so any feedback's good.

I realize this is a bit similar to Scp 682 and others; I'm trying to make it as original as possible. I appreciate any tips or ideas!

I moved and trimmed your thread summary, since it was taking up extra space in the main forum screen. Try to keep thread descriptions (the text in the little box under the thread title) and titles short so you don't crowd out other authors in the forum listing. ~Zyn

Scp 5091 is a boy who died in 1909 but came back to life in his coffin. He suffocated from lack of air, then came back. This went on until the cemetery he was buried in was dug up and he was taken in by the foundation, who conducted a battery of tests on him to see how different causes of death would affect him.

I call him Ressurection Teddy, as a nod to the legend of Resurrection Mary. Does that count as plagiarism?

Seeking Greenlights: Yes

Page Type: SCP Article

Elevator Pitch: This kid isn't any stronger than a normal child, and he can be killed just the same, but nothing will keep him down permanently, even if it takes months for him to recover.

Central Narrative: The different ways the foundation killed him. They've starved him, kept him up for a few months, froze him, burned him, cut him up, poisoned him, introduced him to other Scps such as 053 and 049, and even given him a dish containing shrimp, only to realize he's deathly allergic to the stuff when he went into anaphylactic shock.

+ show block
– hide block

But no matter what happens, he'll come back. Often times he's confused or frightened or just plain pissed, but alive and free of any fatal wounds nonetheless. All these tests have left him traumatized, possibly beyond repair.

During an interview, he asks where his parents are. The doctor tells him they're likely dead, and he has a panic attack and hasn't talked since. Testing was suspended, and the poor thing is being given counseling.

Hook/Attention-Grabber: He can't be killed permanently, at least not in any way that the foundation has discovered.

Additional Notes: The 5091 number is a placeholder, I'll give it another number when I post it to the mainsite.

item.title: Edit SCP or new tale?
item.description: I have an idea for an original character based around SCP-2806, should I edit the existing article to include him as a new instance or write a tale and reference the article?
item.content:encoded:
I have an idea for a character that I have a lot of confidence in, but I want to make sure I introduce him correctly. First impressions matter, and if I do this wrong, it could be the end for him, and maybe me too.

So the idea is a cyborg, but not really a complex cyborg, actually he just has a cybernetic arm. It's a concept I have worked with a lot, and I feel it could work with SCP-2806. I know I could make up something more original, but that entry felt like it had everything I needed to work with and I want to work with the universe rather than forcing it around me. The long term story is that he ends up in Alpha-9, but not because he's the coolest guy in the room, but because he got into a situation where he got the offer and it was either this or amnestics, and frankly it was enough on the edge the Foundation was cool either way. So the interesting part of the story is that this a guy who's saving the world one skip at a time because he was in the wrong place at the wrong time.

Where I'm at I think it would work to edit the original article adding the new instance to the description, adding a new containment procedure for the new instance, and an interview between the agent and the SCP to get some info on what seperated this guy from all the others that just get the Skywalker protocol. Should I do all that, or just post the interview as it's own tale with a reference to the article?

item.title: SCP Idea green light
item.content:encoded:
Seeking Greenlights: Yes

Page Type: SCP Article

Genre (Optional): Drama

Elevator Pitch: 4 unseen ancient lineages of nautiloids are found around the Atlantic Ocean. Each one is drastically different from the other. Not only in physiology, but also in tactics, weapons, and speed.
Though they rarely interact, every five years, one individual from each of these nautiloid lineages will travel to the center of the Bermuda Triangle. After each battle, only one individual will leave the deathmatch.

Central Narrative: Four undiscovered nautiloids species were discovered fighting in the middle of the Bermuda Triangle by an international oceanography survey. They were later discovered in different parts of the Atlantics with little overlap in population overlap.

SCP-XXXX-A are conical-shelled nautiloids resembling Orthoceras in physique. Shell length is 4 meters. The arm length is 1.5 meters each arm. Skin is red with a brown shell. During Autumn, the instances of SCP-XXXX-a will migrate to the southern Atlantic until mid-April.

+ show block
– hide block

SCP-XXXX-B are curved-shelled nautiloids living in the Caribbean. Shell length of the instance is 1.5 meters. A protrusion of iron from a meter up extends 20cm out from the shell. Arms of this instance are a meter long and hooked. Webbing is present between the arms 20cm from the base.

SCP-XXXX-C has a shell diameter of 1 meter. Resembling a form of a modern nautilus. Grooves are present where the walls of the air chambers are located. Skin is mostly navy blue.

SCP-XXXX-D are coiled-shelled nautiloids with a shell diameter of 2 meters. The shell is a gradient of orange and yellow with a black rock outer layer on it. Arms of SCP-XXXX-D instance are retracted and have microscopic hairs. Arms extend to 5 meters when in use.

Every 10 years, a ritual of fertility will be held by each instance of SCP-XXXX at the center of the Bermuda Triangle. The ritual ends until the last instance is alive. The sole survivor of the ritual, for example, an instance of SCP-XXXX-B, will have a population boom of three years for its instance.

Hook/Attention-Grabber: Humans know more of what’s above them than what’s below the deep oceans. The oceans are scary indeed. About 90-97% of the ocean is still undiscovered. The ocean is the last frontier to travel on this planet. Many creatures are left undiscovered to this day.

It'll normally attempt to lure you in by using creatures that trick you into believing that people you trust are asking you to go inside, primarily by shapeshifting. The main creature1 luring you in is trapped inside the house and can create other creatures2 to go outside and lure you in for it if necessary. It will keep trying until it gets tired or finds more suitable prey. Once you're in, you become one of the minions of the main creature inhabiting the house.

Central Narrative: So… some kids messed up. Basically, a kid's grandmother told him about a spell that could curse households. Reason? Not important. What's important is that you can't trust kids with magic. That kid went and told all his friends about it, and they thought it would be funny if they cursed this one house on a mountain.

Oh yeah, did I mention kids are really bad at using magic? In fact, they're so bad that one of the kids in the friend group got cursed along with the house and was forced to inhabit it forever3. After the spell was cast, the Foundation detected anomalous activity on a mountain… somewhere. Haven't decided yet. ¯\_(ツ)_/¯

Anyway, the Foundation took the kids in and gave them amnestics, but… it didn't work. Because of how the curse functions, it wouldn't allow them to forget about it. The Foundation had no choice but to take care of them until they were old enough to become Class-D Personnel.

All of those events set up the Foundation's investigations on why the house was what it was. The Class-D were used for explorations and it revealed more about the grandmother (yeah, remember her?) and her relations to their family's history with magic and anomalies.

Hook/Attention Grabber: I guess it could be the small mistake of some negligent kids unraveling a family's anomalous secrets. The chain reaction could be somewhat interesting.

item.title: Brainstorming - Amber Water
item.content:encoded:
Basically a brainstorming thread for a potential SCP.

The idea behind it involves an SCP that, in its present state at the time of the article, is a tank of amber-colored water. In a solid or liquid state, the water has no special properties other than its unusual color. In a gaseous state, however - particularly a semi-gaseous mist - the water transports whomever travels through it to an oceanic world with no fauna.

Despite this, I'm thinking that the world is very friendly to life - the seas are freshwater, and there's a diverse ecosystem of plant life beneath the surface, some of which are edible and moderately nutritious to humans, despite their alien nature.

The SCP story itself involves an SCP scientist who's sent to investigate the unusual amber cloud hovering about a mile off the coast of Tanzania, when a powerful wind blows it into him before he has time to adjust his course, transporting him to the oceanic world, where he encounters a large sentient cetacean-like creature and a sentient, flying arachnid-like creature. The story itself would explore the backstory of the world, and the interactions of three sentient creatures and how they interact with their environment when they're unequally built for it, and the power dynamic that emerges as a result of their unequal adaptations.

I'm still figuring out the mechanics behind the mist itself, though the fact that it only facilitates transportation as a mist and not in any other state of matter is key to the story's resolution.

Elevator Pitch: A collection of living Gundam models. Have organs underneath the plastic armor plates, but they do not match any living species. The models speak in the memories of American soldiers in the Vietnam War that seem to be from another timeline.

Central Narrative: Tells the story of American soldiers in the Vietnam War. The models were found in a former Vietnamese battlefield with significant damage. On the surface, there is nothing particularly strange about them. However, there appear to be functioning organs beneath the plastic armor plates that do not match up to any known species. Although they appear to be human-like, they contain DNA that varies greatly from those of humans. The living parts of all of the models are of the same species. The models cannot move, but they are known to speak. It speaks from the perspective of several soldiers such as General Richard Hall from the dates of November 8, 1955, to May 9, 1961. It begins with Richard Hall getting drafted, and later the other soldiers are seen getting drafted. The story from here on out consists mostly dialogue between the models, shouting during battles, and various promotions. At any points in time where a bodily fluid would be excreted by one of the soldiers, the model excretes the same fluid. Recorded excretions include blood, sweat, tears, and urine. Although the story encompasses almost seven years, the full seven years are not played out. Only select days are played out. These days include battles, significant interactions, and promotions. The full day is always played out. On the final day, there is a battle that all of the soldiers take part in. In this battle, they each comment on a creature that looks somewhat like a dog before dying. Upon death, they bleed profusely for 5 minutes before the organs cease function. After 214 hours, the story begins again the exact same way, in a cyclical nature. The real versions of these soldiers all had different positions. They all died on July 24, 2006.

Hook/Attention-Grabber: Emotional story told by Gundams.

Central Narrative: A object collides with the moon not far from Lunar Area-32 and a team sets out to investigate it. At the impact site they find a crater with a dark substance from which they take samples and return to base. Further study of the substance shows that it contains a parasite that will enter the human body through a body opening or wound and attach to the brain stem.

Once at the brain stem anomalous effects will start taking place within 24 hours. First the host will start producing the dark substance found at the impact site in its stomach and proceed to vomit it out once it fills up. It's unknown how the substance is created, the human body is not believed to have the necessary elements to create the substance and no other body weight is lost when the substance is created. Secondly the host will begin experiencing time much slower than others. This will only occur when no one has contact with the host and has a devastating effect on the mental health of the hosts. The third anomalous effect starts taking place about 6 months after the parasite enters the body at which point the black substance will stop being produced and time will be perceived normally again for a short time before the subject suddenly dies and several parasites exit the body. The deceased subject will then rapidly decompose as time now passes faster for the body.

Foundation researchers begin experimenting with the idea of using the parasites anomalous effects to their benefit. Some researchers under extreme time pressure to finish some important project could possibly use the time slowing effects of the parasite to conduct large amounts of research in a short time. The problem with this is the quick deterioration of a hosts mental state.

Hook/Attention-Grabber: It's a quite simple story that I hope to make interesting through exploration of the SCP and it's effects, and possibly how it could be used to the foundations benefit.

item.title: Good intentions
item.description: A semi-sentient liquid metal that tries to protect his host
item.content:encoded:
Seeking Greenlights: Yes

Page Type: SCP Article

Elevator Pitch: A semi-sentient liquid metal that bonds with a persons nervous system and tries to protect that person from harm, but ultimately does more harm than good.

Central Narrative: The SCP is an unknown liquid metal that enters a persons body through the skin, bonding with that persons nervous system. Whenever an object/person comes into contact with the skin of the host, the metal will rush through the persons nerves to the point of impact, surfacing out of the skin to form a shield that protects the person from physical trauma. The SCP accidentally damages the nerves when it travels through them, causing intense pain in the host in the short run, and loss of fine motor skills to loss of all feelings in limbs in the long run. Even if the SCP is inactive in the host, over time the host will develop symptoms similar to long-term mercury poisoning, which will result in death after 10-15 months.

+ show
- hide

The SCP will only have one host at a time, and will not transfer to another while the previous host still lives. It initially transfers by skin to skin contact with the previous hosts corpse, however if the SCP is without a host for an extended period of time, it will leave the previous hosts body and seek out the nearest human to bond with. If it is unable to find a host after leaving the previous host, it will become increasingly aggressive and stronger to break out and locate a new host.

Due to the SCP reacting to even the smallest contacts with the skin, it becomes nigh impossible for the host to complete small tasks, and even a small shift in their clothing can set of the SCP. Monitoring the effects the SCP has on its hosts is extremely difficult, because the SCP prevents the foundation from taking any samples while the host still lives, and most forms of scans are ineffective.

In order to contain the anomaly, the foundation will expose a D-class in a medically induced coma to the SCP, and try to keep them alive for as long as possible. After the death of the D-class, a new D-class will be put into a coma before transferring the SCP to them.


Hook/Attention-Grabber: Something created to protect humans ends up damaging them in the long run.

Earworms will hang in bushes and form cacoons in the shape of small music notes, at which point they will begin produce a song.

The Earworm's song compels those who hear it to eat it, at which point, the stomach acids will dissolve the cacoon and Earworm will burrow out of the stomach and make it's way to the brain, burrowing into the left side of the cerebrum then inject an amnestic so the host forgets eating the cacoon. It will remain there in a hibernating state until the host hears music.

+ show block
– hide block

Once the host hears music, the Earworm will awaken and begin eating the hosts Cerebellum, growing in size and connecting to the Host's nervous system. During this process the host will be unable to get the song that activated the earworm out of their head.

Over time, the Earworm will eat and replace more and more of the hosts brain, eventually removing the ability for complex thought and turning the host into a feral creature incapable of speaking in anything other than the song. At this point the Earworm, now resembling brain tissue itself, will lay eggs in the remains of the hosts brain and the host will be drawn to populated yet rural areas. Elevator Pitch: A giant formless fleshy monstrosity living in the a part of the Bering Sea. While immobile, the creature is sentient, and appears to be in a constant state of distress. When a living human victim is fed to the creature, it will expel the remains of its last victim, and its new victim will take over its body until a new one is fed to it.

Central Narrative: After discovering the creature and its property, the Foundation appoints General Ferguson in charge of containment, who quickly begins cracking down on the anomaly. Soon after, it is found that the SCP can communicate in simple sentences via a special radio frequency, and the foundation discovers that the anomaly is "hungry" and "hurting", and wants more victims so it can be freed. After this, Ferguson cracks down even more, building a massive concrete wall around the anomaly and ordering constant security, with no one to be anywhere near the creature or have any communication. While many researchers do attempt communication otherwise, they are unable to do much else to help it due to Ferguson's strict orders. Eventually, a d class ends up being fed to it, and there is a massive call among the other d class at the station to feed it another victim to save their comrade.

Hook/Attention Grabber: After this, Ferguson becomes even more strict, with anyone who sympathizes with the anomaly ordered to be imprisoned for treason against the Foundation. SCP-XXXX-A is capable of being contacted currently through an email which is posted on SCP-XXXX's website. Page Layout (Optional): ACS

Elevator Pitch: SCP is a small, 50m long beach located near Kandestederne, Denmark. In the event an individual makes contact with the sand, it will respond to the conscious thoughts of that individual and shift into a variety of structures accordingly. With concentration, The sand can also emulate the structures physical (not chemical) properties, such as weight, ductility, pigment and conductivity. However, it can't take the form of non-solids. The sand only acts this way if it's on the beach. If the sand is taken 5 meters away from the beach, the sand will start vibrating and pulsating before suddenly becoming inactive. The sand also appears to have some degree of sapience/conscious and can react if communicated with or attacked.

Central Narrative: When the Foundation first discovered the beach (in the 1950s), it was acting aggressive and attacked anyone who attempted to walk upon it. Through research and discussions with the locals, the Foundation discover one of them is in possession of a jar of sand which they took from the beach after discovering it's strange properties. The sand was then returned and the beach instantly began cooperating.

After some experiments with the sand, researchers managed to discover it could understand Koine Greek. After finding a translater, the Foundation were able to discover that the sand is in fact the remnants of the Oread, the mountain nymphs from Greek Mythology. The Oreads reveal that long ago, they lost their true form in a battle with a monstrous sea creature1, resulting in them taking on their current sand from. In their sand form, they're conscious was spread so thin, only they're instinct to join back together remained. This was difficult as their parts were spread across the world via ocean currents. The beach is a collection of their remnants who've managed to form a collective conscious. However, it's weak enough to be influenced by a stronger mind, resulting in the structures it creates.

Hook/Attention-Grabber: This article is kind of sad. We're meant to feel sorry for the Oreads. They desperately want to return to their old forms but The Foundation is unable to help as 1. it would take forever for every sand particle to randomly end up on the beach and 2. how can The Foundation possibly give them back their true form if they don't know who's who and what they look like.

item.title: SCP idea, seeking greenlight: The Grand Conspiracy
item.content:encoded:
Seeking Greenlights: Yes

Page Type: SCP Article

Elevator Pitch: An infohazard that causes no side effects whatsoever unless someone tries to look into the nature of its existence. Anyone who attempts such will become more and more unstable as they begin to obsess over researching the SCP, coming up with theories concerning it that become increasingly irrational as their mental state decreases, eventually driving them to insanity. Essentially, the SCP makes anyone who tries to figure out what it is into a deranged conspiracy theorist.

Central Narrative: The perspective of an unfortunate researcher, showcasing his descent into insanity.

Hook/Attention-Grabber: This SCP isn’t one of those "kills you as soon as you realize it exists" things - it works by lowering your intellect/mental stability until you're not able to even come close to understanding it. For example, an experienced scientist might start off with a somewhat accurate hypothesis, only to wind up believing that it was created by Hitler's secret grandchild in Area 51 a week later. And considering that it has no outward anomalous effects, it could potentially have already infected every person on the planet undetected - alternatively, it could be some kind of virus with a malicious purpose that the Foundation will never be able to come close to discovering.

Additional Notes: I haven't yet figured out some parts of this, like how exactly the Foundation would discover this SCP exists - I can work out the finer details when I start drafting. For now, I just want to know if this would be something people are interested in reading.
